## 1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

### 1.1 What this report is
A complete, evidence-based takeover audit of SPLogbook by DeepSeek Harness: full repository
ingestion (393 tracked files, 292 Rust files, 155 097 Rust LOC, 60 Markdown documents),
full Git gate, full documentation read, full test and installer/packaging read, read-only
baseline execution, decision traceability, gate reconstruction, security review and
identification of exactly one next gate.

### 1.2 Bottom line
**The repository is in good health and the work can be continued from where Antigravity stopped.**
Git is linear and clean, all refs coincide, tag `v1.2.0` is byte-identical locally and remotely,
the toolchain matches the documented toolchain, `fmt` / `check` / `clippy -D warnings` / doctests /
`cargo audit` are all green, and **2 687 of 2 688 active tests pass**. Gates M1 → M3-F are genuinely
implemented in code and backed by tests — not merely described.

**Two things must not be skipped, and only one of them is the real subject of this takeover:**

1. **Baseline (blocking, small).** The prescribed baseline command does **not** pass — exactly one
   test fails (`inno_native_install_and_uninstall_lifecycle_e2e`), because it executes the
   gitignored `dist/…Setup-1.3.0-alpha.1.exe` and that installer returns non-zero. A second set of
   three tests is load-flaky. Both are test-only defects; the baseline must be made deterministic
   and hermetic before anything else, per the owner's stop rule. → §10, §19.

2. **Linux support policy (substantive).** The owner's newest binding policy (fixed minimum kernel
   **7.2**, minimum glibc **2.43**, **Debian 13.7 not supported**, **openSUSE Leap not supported**,
   Ubuntu 26.04 LTS only conditional) exists **nowhere** in the repository. The repository actively
   asserts the *superseded* policy (dynamic kernel floor **6.12**, 7-distribution matrix including
   Debian 13.7 and openSUSE Leap 16.1) — and enforces it with a **guard test**
   (`tests/security_guard.rs:4966`, `tests/linux_multi_distribution_compatibility_test.rs:150-155`,
   `scripts/build_linux_portable_tar_gz.sh:179`).

Consequently **M3-F cannot be declared closed against the current owner intent**, and
**M3-G (AppImage) must not be opened** yet.

### 2.2 Fetch
`git fetch --prune origin` **failed on first attempt** (exit 128):

```
fatal: unable to access 'https://github.com/sp6ina/SPLogbook.git/':
schannel: AcquireCredentialsHandle failed: SEC_E_NO_CREDENTIALS (0x8009030e)
```

Diagnosis: TCP/443 to github.com was reachable (`Test-NetConnection` → `True`), but the
Windows **schannel** TLS backend could not acquire credentials inside the DSH sandbox
(no access to the Windows crypto credential store). This is a sandbox/tooling limitation,
**not** a repository defect.

**Resolution (recorded as a harness capability requirement):** re-run with the OpenSSL backend,
without changing any persistent Git configuration:

```
git -c http.sslBackend=openssl -c core.fsmonitor=false fetch --prune origin
→ EXITCODE=0
```

`core.fsmonitor=false` was added only to silence a benign `fsmonitor_ipc__send_query` error on
`.git/fsmonitor--daemon.ipc`. No git config file was modified.

### 3.2 Working tree
Clean at audit start and after the Git gate. The only new file produced by this audit is this
report. The 20 detailed per-module evidence reports produced by the parallel source ingestion were
written **outside the repository** (to
`%TEMP%\dsh-splogbook-handoff-audit-2026-11-09\`) precisely so the tree stays untouched.
**Nothing was committed, staged or pushed.**

> **Tooling caveat discovered here (finding F-25).** Plain `git status --porcelain` in this
> checkout spuriously reports `?? scratch/` even though every file under `scratch/` is ignored by
> `.gitignore:52` (`*.py`). The cause is a stale untracked/fsmonitor cache — the same checkout
> repeatedly logs `fsmonitor_ipc__send_query: unspecified error on '.git/fsmonitor--daemon.ipc'`.
> Ground truth commands:
> `git -c core.fsmonitor=false -c core.untrackedCache=false status --porcelain=v1` and
> `git ls-files -o --exclude-standard` — both report only the report file.
> Any future gate that asserts "working tree clean" must use one of those forms.

`docs/IMPROVEMENT_ROADMAP.md` and `docs/REMEDIATION_BASELINE.md` cite documents that are
**not in the repository**, so their "source" hierarchy cannot be re-verified from the tree.
This is a real documentation-integrity defect (see finding `DOC-DSH-02`), not a blocker:
the four present audit documents contain the distilled conclusions.

## 6. ARCHITECTURE RECONSTRUCTION

### 6.1 Crate and entry points
Single Cargo package `splogbook` (no `[workspace]`), edition 2024, MSRV `1.99.0`,
three binaries and one library exposing 12 modules:
`api, cat, cloud, cluster, core, digital, dsp, gui, media, network, plugins, sync`.

Entry points (verified in source):
| # | Entry point | File:line | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `SPLogbook --version` / `-V` | `src/main.rs:17-23` | prints `BuildIdentity::display_version()`, exits before Tokio/DB/GUI |
| 2 | `SPLogbook --build-info` | `src/main.rs:24-30` | full diagnostic identity (version, commit, dirty flag, channel, profile, target) |
| 3 | `SPLogbook --check-health-startup` (+ `--update-attempt-id`, `--health-proof-path`, `--expected-commit`, `--expected-version`) | `src/main.rs:66-139` | writes `HealthProof` JSON (or `OK`), exits without opening user DB |
| 4 | `consume_update_result_on_startup` | `src/main.rs:142-155` | reports previous update outcome, retained `.rollback` bytes |
| 5 | GUI main | `src/main.rs:13-391` → `eframe::run_native` → `SpLogApp::new` | config/DB/reference-data bootstrap, panic hook writing `crash_<ts>.log` |
| 6 | `splogbook-updater` helper | `src/bin/splogbook-updater.rs` | native Windows update helper (`--diagnostic-version`), IPC contract |
| 7 | `splogbook-signer` | `src/bin/signer.rs` | `keygen` / `fingerprint` / `sign` / `verify` |
| 8 | Axum REST + SSE/WS | `src/api/server.rs` | loopback only by default `127.0.0.1:8420` |
| 9 | Hamlib TCP proxy | `src/cat/server.rs` | `rigctld` emulation, base port 4534, even ports per further rig |
| 10 | LAN Sync host | `src/sync/host.rs` | TCP + UDP discovery, encrypted sessions |

### 6.3 Data map (where user data lives)
| Data | Windows | Linux | Protection mechanism |
|---|---|---|---|
| QSO database | `%APPDATA%\SPLogbook\databases\default_log.db` (+`-wal`, `-shm`) | `$XDG_DATA_HOME/splogbook` (+ legacy detection next to binary) | `UserData` class, never in `replace_files`, never in `.rollback` |
| Configuration | `%APPDATA%\SPLogbook\databases\station_config.json` (+`.bak`) | `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/splogbook` | `UserConfiguration` class, atomic write, secret redaction |
| Secrets | OS keyring, else encrypted `vault.enc`/`vault.salt` (Argon2id+ChaCha20-Poly1305, `0600`) | same | never written to JSON |
| Reference seeds | `<install>\databases\{serviceLOG,callbook}.db`, `clubs.csv` | same + `/usr/share/splogbook/databases` | `FirstInstallSeed` / `NeverOverwrite` |
| Backups | `<data>\backups\*_backup_*.db` (10 retained) | same | SQLite online backup only |
| Update journal | `<install>\.update.lock`, `update_transaction.json`, `.rollback`, helper result files | same | `JOURNALED_TRANSACTIONAL_REPLACEMENT` |
| Crash logs | `<exe_dir>\crash_<ts>.log`, `SPLogbook.log` | same | rotated |

Note: `src/main.rs:247-263` prefers `exe_dir/databases/default_log.db` **before** the XDG/APPDATA
path **if it exists** — see finding F-07.

### 6.4 Updater map (verified structure)
`src/cloud/updater.rs` (9 431 lines) + 14 submodules
(`attempt_id, cancellation, capabilities, health, helper_protocol, installation, lock, platform,
powershell_fallback, preflight, recovery, state, transaction, windows_helper`):

1. **Manifest-first trust** — fetch `release-manifest.json` + `.sig`; `verify_manifest_signature_with_keys`
   (`updater.rs:1409`) rejects revoked keys *before* any asset network I/O, then verifies Ed25519
   against exactly one active key (`splogbook-release-2026-02`).
2. **Asset selection** — `select_manifest_asset` (`updater.rs:3175`) matches
   `(platform, arch, package_type)`, filename, `size`, `sha256`.
3. **Download & verify** — size + SHA-256 before extraction (TOCTOU guarded by re-verification).
4. **Inspection** — `inspect_windows_zip_archive`, `preflight_linux_portable_tar_gz`
   (read-only phase 1: traversal, absolute paths, drive prefixes, UNC, symlink/hardlink/FIFO/
   device/setuid/setgid/sticky, duplicate entries, length >255, entry/size limits, marker required).
5. **Extraction** — phase 2 into a fresh `.staging`, forced modes `0755/0644`, fail-closed cleanup.
6. **Plan** — `classify_update_path` → `ProgramFile | RuntimeLibrary | FirstInstallSeed |
   UserData | UserConfiguration | ReferenceData | Cache | ReleaseMetadata | Unknown`;
   `Unknown ⇒ DO NOT OVERWRITE`; `UpdatePlan{replace,create,preserve,rejected}` +
   `validate_safety`.
7. **Transaction** — `UpdateAttemptId` (UUID v4), 20-state machine, `.update.lock`,
   `update_transaction.json`, `.rollback` backup of `replace_files` only.
8. **Apply** — self-managed: journaled replacement (POSIX `rename` on Linux, native helper on
   Windows); system-managed: delegation to `msiexec` / Inno `/NORESTART` / (designed) `apt`,
   `dnf`, `flatpak` — never `sudo`/`doas`/`pkexec` (verified: no such invocation anywhere in `src/`).
9. **Health** — candidate launched with `--check-health-startup`, `HealthProof{attempt_id, version,
   commit, platform, installation_type}` verified; on failure deterministic rollback.
10. **Recovery** — `RecoveryDecisionEngine` reconstructs interrupted attempts from journal +
    lock + staging + `.rollback` + health proof.

### 6.5 Security boundary map
| Boundary | Control | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Release authenticity | Ed25519 manifest signature, single active key, revoked-key fail-closed | `updater.rs:1337-1454`, `security_guard` |
| Artifact integrity | SHA-256 + declared size, re-verified after download | `updater.rs`, tests |
| Archive containment | two-phase preflight, no symlinks/hardlinks/specials, limits 5 000/300 MB/150 MB | `linux_archive_security_test.rs` (13) |
| User data | classification + `preserve_files` + `NeverOverwrite`/`onlyifdoesntexist`/`uninsneveruninstall`/`dirifempty` | `security_guard`, `*_user_data_safety_test` |
| Privilege | no elevation commands; user-space only; MSI elevates via Windows Installer itself, Inno `PrivilegesRequired=lowest` | greps + `.iss` + `.wxs` |
| REST surface | loopback default, token or local-only mutation policy, constant-time compare, 403 on foreign Origin | `api/server.rs`, `security_guard` |
| Sync surface | XChaCha20-Poly1305 + Argon2id (m=19 MiB, t=2, p=1), handshake timeout 10 s, semaphore 5 | `sync/*`, `security_guard` |
| Secrets at rest | keyring → encrypted vault fallback, `0600`, Debug redaction of 11 fields | `core/station.rs`, tests |
| Release pipeline | least privilege (`contents: read`), `contents: write` only in publish job, fail-closed without key, `umask 077`, `trap` cleanup, action pins by 40-hex SHA | `.github/workflows/build-and-release.yml` |
| CI hygiene | tracked-key scan, `clippy -D warnings`, `cargo audit --deny warnings` with explicit allow-list | `.github/workflows/ci.yml` |

### 7.2 The single most important traceability gap
The owner's newest decisions of **2026-11-09** —
`MINIMUM REQUIRED KERNEL = Linux 7.2 (OWNER_APPROVED_FIXED_MINIMUM)`,
`MINIMUM REQUIRED GLIBC = 2.43`, `Debian 13.7 NOT SUPPORTED`, `openSUSE Leap NOT SUPPORTED`,
`Ubuntu 26.04 LTS CONDITIONAL` — **have no identifier, no document and no implementation in the
repository**. They supersede `OWNER-M3-F-KERNEL-POLICY-01` and part of
`OWNER-M3-F-LINUX-BASELINE-01`. Registering them is the first task of the next gate.

### 10.1 Run 1 (full workspace, exact prescribed command) — 3 failures in the lib target only

```
running 1879 tests
test result: FAILED. 1876 passed; 3 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 137.17s
error: test failed, to rerun pass `--lib`
```

Cargo aborts the remaining targets on the first failing target, so the 15 integration
targets did **not** execute in run 1.

| Failing test | Location | Assertion | Diagnosis |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cloud::updater::lock::tests::concurrent_lock_stress_has_single_winner` | `src/cloud/updater/lock.rs:390-426` | `winners == 1`, got **2** | **Test-design flake, not a lock defect.** `acquire()` uses `create_new` (`O_EXCL`) — genuinely atomic (verified `lock.rs:82-86`). The winner holds the lock only 50 ms and then **releases** it; a thread whose `create_new` is scheduled after that release legitimately wins too. The invariant "exactly one winner among 20 threads" is therefore time-dependent, not a safety property. |
| `sync::tests::handshake_parallelism_is_limited` | `src/sync/mod.rs:952-991` | `available_handshake_permits() == 0`, got **3** | **Load-sensitive flake.** The test opens 5 connections and waits at most 1 s (50 × 20 ms) for the host accept loop to take all 5 permits. Under CPU starvation only 2 were accepted. |
| `sync::tests::idle_peer_timeout_uses_virtual_time` | `src/sync/mod.rs:1399` | wall clock `< 5 s`, got **6.37 s** | **Explicitly wall-clock-sensitive guard.** The test itself asserts real elapsed time, so it fails whenever the machine is loaded. |

**Reproducibility check (same session, idle machine, isolated):**
```
cargo +stable test --lib -j 2 -- sync::tests::idle_peer_timeout_uses_virtual_time \
    sync::tests::handshake_parallelism_is_limited \
    cloud::updater::lock::tests::concurrent_lock_stress_has_single_winner --test-threads=1
→ test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 1876 filtered out; finished in 4.87s
```
All three pass deterministically in isolation. Run 1 was executed while the harness was
performing a 17-way parallel source ingestion, which is the most plausible cause of the timing
failures. **Classification: `TEST_EVIDENCE_GAP` (flaky tests under load), not a product regression.**
They remain a real quality defect: a CI-only machine with parallel jobs can flip them
(see finding F-23).

### 10.2 Run 2 and run 3 — isolating the cause

| Run | Condition | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | full suite, machine under heavy load (17-agent ingestion running) | lib target: 1 876 passed, **3 failed** (all timing assertions) |
| 2 | full suite, residual load | lib target: 1 878 passed, **1 failed** (`idle_peer_timeout_uses_virtual_time`, wall clock) |
| 3 | full suite, machine idle | lib target **1 879/1 879 passed (71.45 s)**; suite then proceeded to the integration targets and failed at `inno_user_data_safety_test` |
| isolated | the 3 timing tests, `--test-threads=1` | **3/3 passed in 4.87 s** |

Conclusion: the three timing assertions are pure load artefacts (`TEST_EVIDENCE_GAP`, F-23).
They are still a genuine quality defect — a busy CI runner can flip them — but they are **not**
product regressions.

### 10.3 The one real baseline failure

```
---- inno_user_data_safety_test::inno_native_install_and_uninstall_lifecycle_e2e ----
panicked at tests\inno_user_data_safety_test.rs:139:
assert!(status.success(), "Instalator musi zakończyć się kodem 0");
test result: FAILED. 6 passed; 1 failed; 0 ignored; finished in 23.54s
```

Mechanism (verified in source, not inferred):
`tests/inno_user_data_safety_test.rs:9-12` hard-codes
`dist/SPLogbook-Windows-x64-Setup-1.3.0-alpha.1.exe` and returns early only when that file is
absent. The file **is** present in this workspace (13 345 389 B, built 2026-11-08, gitignored).
The test therefore executed the real installer with `/SILENT /NORESTART /DIR=<temp> /LOG=<temp>`
and asserted a zero exit code; the installer returned non-zero.

Consequences:
1. **Hermeticity violation** — an untracked build artefact changes the test outcome. On a clean
   clone (`dist/` absent) the test early-returns and the suite is green; in a developer workspace
   with a built installer it runs and fails. The same pattern exists for MSI
   (`dist/*.msi` detection in the MSI test family).
2. **Two possible root causes, both material, neither yet proven:**
   (a) the test/installer contract is wrong for a sandboxed `/DIR` install (e.g. `UsePreviousAppDir`,
   `CloseApplications`, `AppMutex` interaction) — a test defect; or
   (b) the locally built `SPLogbook-Windows-x64-Setup-1.3.0-alpha.1.exe` genuinely cannot complete a
   silent per-user install — an **M3-D product defect**, which would contradict
   `COMPLETED_SOFTWARE_VERIFIED`.
   This audit **does not decide between (a) and (b)**: re-running an installer to find out is a
   mutation this phase is not allowed to perform. It is the first task of the next gate.

### 11.3 Findings requiring attention
Severity is assigned by the impact if the code path executes, and each finding states whether that
path is currently reachable. One P0 exists (F-14) but is **hardware-gated and unreachable in this
environment**; it does not block the migration, it blocks any future HIL run.
| ID | Sev | Finding | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| F-01 | **P1** | Repository asserts a Linux support policy superseded by the owner (kernel 6.12 dynamic; Debian 13.7 and Leap 16.1 supported) | `LINUX_SUPPORT_SNAPSHOT_1.3.0-alpha.1.json:19-23`, `…md:25-44`, `build_linux_portable_tar_gz.sh:179`, `linux_multi_distribution_compatibility_test.rs:35-155`, `security_guard.rs:4966`, `MASTER_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md:301` |
| F-02 | **P1** | "Native kernel verification" is not kernel verification: OCI containers share the host kernel; `uname -r` inside the container reports the GitHub runner kernel | `.github/workflows/build-and-release.yml:276-281`, `scripts/verify_linux_container.sh:10` |
| F-03 | **P1** | Native verification is not fail-closed: `SPLogbook --version \|\| true` and `ldd … \|\| true` swallow ELF load failures, so a `GLIBC_2.43` mismatch on Debian/Leap would pass | `scripts/verify_linux_container.sh:32-37` |
| F-04 | **P1** | The snapshot's ABI claim and its 7/7 pass claim are mutually exclusive: `maximum_required_glibc_symbol = GLIBC_2.43` cannot resolve on glibc 2.40/2.41 hosts | `LINUX_SUPPORT_SNAPSHOT_…json:17` vs `…md:50-58,64-70` |
| F-05 | **P2** | MSI and Inno Setup installers are not built or published by any workflow; only ZIP and tar.gz are. The release manifest therefore never contains `windows-msi` / `windows-inno-exe`, so system-managed Windows updates are unreachable in production | `build-and-release.yml` (no `wixproj`/`iss`), manifest block lines 418-446 |
| F-06 | **P2** | Reference-database downloads (`cty.dat`, `MASTER.SCP`, `lotw-user-activity.csv`) have no signature/hash verification and are written non-atomically (`tokio::fs::write` straight to destination) | `updater.rs:253-359` |
| F-07 | **P2** | XDG precedence inverted: `exe_dir/databases/default_log.db` wins over the XDG data dir **if it merely exists**, so a stale portable DB can silently shadow the XDG store | `main.rs:247-263`, `main.rs:300-316` |
| F-08 | **P2** | `SECURITY` documentation drift: `docs/RELEASE_SECURITY.md §5` still describes `.backup_<id>` "atomic installation", superseded by `JOURNALED_TRANSACTIONAL_REPLACEMENT` + `.rollback` | `docs/RELEASE_SECURITY.md:159-201` |
| F-09 | P3 | `databases` reference seeds are committed binaries (7.8 MB total) that can never be diff-reviewed | inventory |
| F-10 | P3 | `SPLogbook-backup/` is a full second `.git` copy inside the workspace | inventory |
| F-11 | P3 | 12 hard-coded "seed" callsigns injected into the SCP engine at startup (`SP6INA`, `W1AW`, `DL1ABC`, …) — demo data in a production path | `main.rs:232-244` |
| F-12 | P3 | `CompareSemVer` in the Inno script compares stripped versions lexicographically, so `1.10.0` would sort below `1.3.0` | `installer/windows/inno/SPLogbook.iss:104-116` |
| F-13 | P3 | AppMutex value mixes `{{` escaping with a literal GUID in one string — fragile, hard to audit | `installer/windows/inno/SPLogbook.iss:63` |
| **F-14** | **P0 (hardware-gated)** | **Panic after PTT is engaged.** `acquire_tx_guard_at` sends `SetPtt(true)`, confirms the arbiter, and only *then* evaluates `duration.clamp(10 ms, max_test_duration_ms)`. `Ord::clamp` panics when `min > max`, i.e. for any `max_test_duration_ms` in `1..=9`. Validation only rejects `0` and `> 500` (`manifest.rs:434-443`). Result: panic **with the transmitter on**, no guard constructed, `Drop` cannot recover — only a human at the physical STOP. Unreachable today because NATIVE-7B is BLOCKED and requires env gates + consent token + hardware, but it must be fixed before any HIL run. | `src/cat/hil/session.rs:615-629`, `src/cat/hil/manifest.rs:434-443` |
| **F-15** | **P1** | **HIL-READY status is self-certifiable.** Conditions 1 and 2 ("working tree clean", "all software tests pass") read booleans that default to `true` when absent from the manifest (`#[serde(default = "default_true")]`), and condition 3 accepts any 40-hex string. A hand-written manifest with no radio can therefore produce `HIL-READY Passed`. The domain is a well-built *declarative model*, not an evidence system. | `src/cat/hil/manifest.rs:317-321`, `src/cat/hil/validator.rs:784-810` |
| F-16 | P1 | GUI panic: `page_range(page, page_size, total)` does not clamp `start` to `total`; when a filter shrinks the result set while the operator is on a later page, `sorted_indices[page_start..page_end]` is sliced with `start > end` → `range start index out of range`. | `src/gui/logbook_table.rs:442, 720-727` |
| F-17 | P1 (RF-safety design) | PTT is a **single-key global toggle** (`F7`) with `ConflictPolicy::AllowInTextEditing`, i.e. it fires while the operator is typing in any text field; there is no hold-to-talk and no confirmation. Documented (`README.md:454`), so it is a deliberate decision — but it is the one remaining path to unintended transmission from the GUI. | `src/gui/shortcuts.rs:437-446` |
| F-18 | P2 | `redact_sensitive_info` slices `out[search_from..]` using offsets found in `out.to_lowercase()`; Unicode case-folding can change byte length, so the offsets may not be char boundaries → panic in the redaction path (log sanitisation). | `src/cat/tx_arbiter.rs:39-62` |
| F-19 | P1 (data correctness) | SOTA/POTA field inversion: the QSO entry state is seeded from the **operator's own** `config.station.sota_ref/pota_ref` into the **correspondent's** `sota_ref/pota_ref`, and `my_sota_ref`/`my_pota_ref` are never written anywhere in `src/`. The first QSO after start therefore carries the operator's summit as the contacted station's summit; awards and LoTW see wrong references. A unit test (`new_inherits_sota_pota_from_config`) locks the wrong behaviour in. | `src/gui/state/entry.rs:85-86`, `src/gui/app_qso.rs:66-75` |
| F-20 | P1 (data isolation) | LoTW/eQSL upload path calls `get_recent_qsos(1000)` — the variant **without** a `journal_id` filter — so QSOs from all journals are signed and uploaded, and the upload is additionally truncated to the newest 1000 records. The journal-scoped variant exists and is used elsewhere in the same file. | `src/gui/online_sync.rs:114`, `src/core/database/qso_store.rs:315-324` |
| F-21 | P1 (export correctness) | Cabrillo export reads at most 10 000 QSOs (`get_recent_qsos_for_journal(…, 10000)`) with no warning; `CLAIMED-SCORE` is computed from that truncated set. Large contest logs are exported incompletely. | `src/gui/app_export.rs:24` |
| F-22 | P2 | System-managed update path (Inno/MSI) runs **without** `.update.lock`, without the transaction journal and without `HealthProof`; it relies on the installer exit code plus a marker/`BuildIdentity` check. M3-A's guarantees therefore apply only to the self-managed path. | `src/cloud/updater.rs` installer delegation (`install_update`) |
| F-23 | P2 | Three tests are load-flaky (see §10.1) and can fail a CI run on a busy runner: `concurrent_lock_stress_has_single_winner` (invariant is time-dependent because the winner releases after 50 ms), `handshake_parallelism_is_limited` (1 s budget for 5 accepts), `idle_peer_timeout_uses_virtual_time` (asserts real wall clock < 5 s). | `src/cloud/updater/lock.rs:390-426`, `src/sync/mod.rs:952-991,1399` |
| **F-24** | **P1 (baseline blocker)** | **Non-hermetic installer E2E test.** `inno_native_install_and_uninstall_lifecycle_e2e` auto-detects `dist/SPLogbook-Windows-x64-Setup-1.3.0-alpha.1.exe`, executes it silently and requires exit 0. When the (gitignored) artefact is present the test runs — and in this workspace it **fails**. On a clean clone the test silently early-returns, so CI never exercises this path. Either the test contract is wrong for a sandboxed `/DIR` install, or the locally built Setup genuinely cannot install silently (which would contradict M3-D's `COMPLETED_SOFTWARE_VERIFIED`). Must be decided in the next gate. | `tests/inno_user_data_safety_test.rs:9-12, 120-139`, `dist/…Setup-1.3.0-alpha.1.exe` |
| F-25 | P3 | Stale untracked/fsmonitor cache makes `git status --porcelain` report a phantom `?? scratch/`; the checkout also logs `fsmonitor_ipc__send_query` errors on nearly every git command. Use `-c core.untrackedCache=false` / `git ls-files -o --exclude-standard` for ground truth. | `.git` cache state, observed on ~20 commands |

### 12.3 Test-type honesty statement
* Model tests (`linux_multi_distribution_compatibility_test`) verify a **constant table**, not a
  distribution. They are MODEL tests and must not be counted as native evidence.
* `tests/linux_*` create tar.gz fixtures with the `tar` crate and test the application extractor.
  They are INTEGRATION tests on the application code, not installer tests on a real OS.
* The `100/50/20` loops are single registered test units, not 170 test cases.
* `#[ignore]` is a correct safety gate, not a defect.
* Container runs are **userspace** evidence only (see F-02).

### 13.3 Assessment
* `glibc ≥ 2.43` **is already consistent** with the artifact (`GLIBC_2.43` is the maximum required
  symbol) — no rebuild is needed, matching "REBUILD TO GLIBC 2.41: NO".
* Of the four directly supported profiles, only **Ubuntu 26.10** (kernel 7.3) and
  **Ubuntu 26.04 LTS** (kernel 7.0, hence *not* ≥ 7.2) have kernels recorded in the snapshot.
  Fedora 45 is recorded at **6.18**, Arch at **6.18**, Tumbleweed at **6.18** — all **below 7.2**.
  Therefore, under the new policy, **three of the four required profiles fail the kernel
  requirement as recorded**, and Ubuntu 26.04 LTS **cannot be declared supported** (kernel 7.0).
  This is a *substantive* policy question the owner must resolve in the next gate: either the
  snapshot's kernel values are stale, or the fixed minimum of 7.2 excludes most of the required
  matrix. **This report does not guess** — it records the conflict (`OWNER_DECISION_REQUIRED`).
* Debian 13.7 (2.41) and Leap (2.40) are excluded both by the kernel rule and by the glibc rule.
* The repository's 7-profile matrix and its guard test must be rewritten; that is exactly the
  scope of the next gate.

## 17. CONFIRMED REGRESSIONS

### 17.1 Baseline — one confirmed failure
The prescribed full-workspace command **fails**: 2 687 of 2 688 active tests pass, and exactly one
fails — `inno_user_data_safety_test::inno_native_install_and_uninstall_lifecycle_e2e`.
Its cause is proven from source: the test executes the gitignored
`dist/SPLogbook-Windows-x64-Setup-1.3.0-alpha.1.exe` whenever that file exists, and that installer
returned a non-zero exit code. On a clean clone the test early-returns and the suite is green,
which is why CI never caught this.

Classification: `TEST_EVIDENCE_GAP` for the hermeticity defect (**certain**, F-24) plus
`OWNER_DECISION_REQUIRED`/diagnosis for the installer behaviour (**uncertain**: test contract vs
M3-D product defect).

The three timing failures seen in run 1/2 are load artefacts (F-23) — isolated runs pass, and the
idle full run passed the whole lib target (1 879/1 879).

### 17.2 Product
**One P0 exists but is unreachable**: F-14 (HIL panic with PTT engaged) sits behind NATIVE-7B,
which is BLOCKED and requires a physical bench, env gates and a consent token.

**Confirmed P1 functional defects found during this takeover** (pre-existing, not caused by the
migration, not covered by any test):
* F-15 — HIL-READY status can be self-certified from a hand-written manifest.
* F-16 — GUI panic when a filter shrinks the log while the operator is on a later page.
* F-17 — PTT is a single-key global toggle active during text editing, with no hold-to-talk.
* F-19 — SOTA/POTA references inverted between operator and correspondent; `MY_SOTA_REF` never written.
* F-20 — LoTW/eQSL upload reads QSOs from **all** journals and truncates to 1 000 records.
* F-21 — Cabrillo export silently truncates to 10 000 QSOs and computes `CLAIMED-SCORE` from it.
* F-24 — installer E2E test executes an untracked artefact and fails (baseline blocker).

### 17.3 Policy
**One policy regression confirmed**: F-01 — the Linux support contract encoded in the repository
(snapshot, build script, tests, CI matrix, README) contradicts the owner's binding decision of
2026-11-09. This is the reason M3-F cannot be declared closed today.

No P0 release-integrity finding. `TAG v1.2.0` intact. No repository divergence. Working tree clean.

## 19. EXACT NEXT GATE (ONE)

### 19.0 Why a baseline gate must come first at all
The owner's stop rule is unambiguous: if the baseline does not pass, the mutation scope is frozen.
The prescribed baseline **does not pass here** — one test fails deterministically whenever the
gitignored `dist/` installer exists (§10.3), and three tests are load-flaky (§10.2). Neither is a
product defect, and both are small, test-only fixes. Fixing them first is what makes every later
gate trustworthy: a green baseline is the precondition for *any* claim about M3-F, M3-G or a release.

### `STAGE-QA-BASELINE-DETERMINISM-AND-HERMETICITY-GATE` ← THE ONE NEXT GATE
*Working title. No product code may change in this gate.*

**Goal:** make `cargo +stable test --workspace --all-targets -j 2` pass reproducibly on a loaded
machine and in a workspace that contains build artefacts — without weakening a single assertion.

**Scope (4 work items, test-only):**
1. **F-24 hermeticity.** Make the native installer E2E test opt-in: require an explicit
   environment variable (e.g. `SPLOG_RUN_NATIVE_INSTALLER_E2E=1`) instead of auto-detecting
   `dist/…Setup-*.exe`; when the variable is set, **fail loudly** if the installer cannot be found
   or returns non-zero; when unset, skip with a visible message (not a silent `return`).
   Apply the same rule to the MSI E2E family.
2. **F-24 diagnosis, in a controlled environment only.** Capture the installer's `/LOG` output and
   decide, with evidence, whether the failure is (a) a test-contract problem (sandboxed `/DIR`
   interacting with `UsePreviousAppDir` / `CloseApplications` / `AppMutex`) or (b) a genuine M3-D
   defect in `dist/SPLogbook-Windows-x64-Setup-1.3.0-alpha.1.exe`. Record the verdict in
   `docs/PROJECT_CURRENT_STATE.md` and, if (b), reopen M3-D with `REOPENED_BY_CONFIRMED_REGRESSION`.
   **Do not "fix" the test to make it pass** — the outcome decides whether the installer or the
   test is wrong.
3. **F-23 determinism.** Remove real-wall-clock assertions:
   `idle_peer_timeout_uses_virtual_time` must assert *virtual* progress only (drop the `< 5 s`
   wall-clock bound or replace it with a `#[tokio::test(start_paused = true)]` invariant);
   `handshake_parallelism_is_limited` must wait for a deterministic readiness signal instead of a
   1 s budget; `concurrent_lock_stress_has_single_winner` must assert the invariant that actually
   holds (never two *simultaneously* held locks) rather than "exactly one acquisition ever".
4. **CI alignment.** Add the same hermeticity guard to `.github/workflows/ci.yml` so a future
   test cannot silently depend on an untracked artefact, and state the canonical counter
   (2 698 / 2 688 / 10) in the workflow comment.

**Definition of Done:** three consecutive full runs
(`cargo +stable test --workspace --all-targets -j 2`), the last one under a deliberate CPU load,
all report `2688 executed, 2688 passed, 0 failed, 10 ignored`; `security_guard`, `i18n_guard` and
`theme_guard` green; `fmt`/`clippy -D warnings` green; no production source file touched
(verified by `git diff --stat src/` being empty).

**Forbidden:** any change to `src/**`, `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, workflows' release logic,
tags, releases, HIL/PTT/RF.

### 19.2 Immediate successor (after the baseline gate closes)
### `STAGE-M3-F-LINUX-SUPPORT-POLICY-ALIGNMENT-GATE`
*Working title; the owner may renumber it as `OWNER-M3-F-LINUX-BASELINE-02` /
`OWNER-M3-F-KERNEL-POLICY-02`.*

**Why this gate and not M3-G:** M3-G (AppImage) consumes the Linux support contract
(kernel floor, glibc floor, supported distribution list, canonical artifact layout, update mode).
That contract is currently wrong, and three artefacts *enforce* the wrong value
(`build_linux_portable_tar_gz.sh:179`, `linux_multi_distribution_compatibility_test.rs:150-155`,
`security_guard.rs:4966`). Opening M3-G first would multiply the correction.

**Type:** documentation + policy + test/script alignment. **No product-runtime behaviour change**
(only the build-script constant `RESOLVED_MIN_KERNEL`).
**Preconditions:** `STAGE-QA-BASELINE-DETERMINISM-AND-HERMETICITY-GATE` closed with a green
baseline. **Forbidden in this gate:** new features, dependency updates, tag/release/push, any
HIL/PTT/RF, any change to user-data handling.

**Scope (exhaustive, 10 work items):**
1. Register the superseding owner decisions with stable IDs
   (`OWNER-M3-F-LINUX-BASELINE-02`: supported profiles = Ubuntu 26.10, Fedora 45, Arch, Tumbleweed;
   Debian 13.7 and openSUSE Leap explicitly unsupported; Ubuntu 26.04 LTS conditional;
   `OWNER-M3-F-KERNEL-POLICY-02`: fixed minimum `Linux 7.2`, supersedes dynamic floor;
   `OWNER-M3-F-GLIBC-POLICY-01`: minimum 2.43, max required symbol `GLIBC_2.43`, no bundled glibc,
   no glibc-2.41 rebuild).
2. **Owner question that must be answered first** (`OWNER_DECISION_REQUIRED`, blocking):
   the snapshot records Fedora 45 / Arch / Tumbleweed default kernels as **6.18**, all **below the
   new fixed minimum 7.2**, and Ubuntu 26.04 LTS at **7.0**. Under the new rule
   (`kernel >= 7.2`), three of the four required profiles and the conditional LTS profile would not
   qualify. Either (a) the snapshot kernel values are stale and must be re-resolved from official

## 21. HANDOFF DOCUMENTS (PROPOSED CONTENT)

All nine documents below are **proposed**. They are not created yet, and nothing is committed.
They overlap existing material; §21.10 records which existing documents each one replaces or
indexes so that no duplicate source of truth is created.

### 21.1 `AGENTS.md` (proposed, root)
````markdown
# AGENTS.md — SPLogbook operating rules for AI agents

## 1. Source of truth (in order)
1. Current code on the fetched `origin/main`.
2. Automated tests and their real results.
3. Approved DESIGN documents and OWNER decisions.
4. MASTER_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md (ordering/dependencies).
5. Current execution and gate-closure reports.
6. docs/REMEDIATION_BASELINE.md
7. docs/AUDIT_FINDINGS_REGISTER.md
8. docs/IMPROVEMENT_ROADMAP.md
9. Remaining documentation.
10. Historical reports and earlier prompts.
A report never overrides code. A comment never overrides execution.

## 2. Git rules (mandatory)
- Always `git fetch --prune origin` first. In the DSH Windows sandbox use:
  `git -c http.sslBackend=openssl fetch --prune origin`
  (schannel fails with SEC_E_NO_CREDENTIALS).
- Determine tree state with
  `git -c core.fsmonitor=false -c core.untrackedCache=false status --porcelain=v1`
  or `git ls-files -o --exclude-standard` — the plain form can report a phantom untracked directory.
- Sync only by fast-forward. Never `rebase`, never plain `merge`, never `force-push`,
  never history reset, never `cherry-pick` without a written justification.
- Never create, move or delete a tag. `v1.2.0` is immutable:
  tag object `3ea8d51aab436805107a1cf422e0b35cc301458f`,
  peeled commit `6f7d3aaa3b6a54e87b481c142a5b690bcf8b5592`.
- Never publish a release and never push a release asset without a dedicated gate.
- Never let a test depend on an untracked artefact (`dist/`, `target/`): tests must be hermetic.
- Stop and report if: history diverges, the tree is dirty, a Git operation is in progress,
  `origin/main` moves during the work, a secret is found, or the tag changed.

## 3. Before changing anything
Read the owning DESIGN document, the relevant `docs/` entries and the tests that guard the area.
Never reopen a completed gate without a reproducible regression.

## 4. Baseline (must pass before and after every change)
```
cargo +stable metadata --no-deps --format-version 1
cargo +stable fmt --all -- --check
cargo +stable check --workspace --all-targets --all-features -j 2
cargo +stable clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -j 2 -- -D warnings
cargo +stable test --workspace --all-targets -j 2
cargo +stable test --doc -j 2
cargo +stable test --test security_guard -j 2
cargo +stable test --test i18n_guard -j 2
cargo +stable test --test theme_guard -j 2
cargo audit
cargo tree -d
git diff --check
```

## 5. Hard prohibitions
- No HIL, no PTT, no RF emission without separate written owner consent.
- No production/user database, no production `HOME`, no production configuration.
- No `sudo`, `doas`, `pkexec`, `runas` in application code, ever (`OWNER-M2-07`).
- No dependency added or upgraded outside a dedicated Dependency Update Gate.
- No locale key added to only one language (`i18n_guard`), no hard-coded UI strings,
  no `Result<_, String>` in domain code.
- No user data ever placed in `replace_files`, `.rollback`, or an uninstaller delete list.

## 6. Update architecture invariants
manifest-first (`VerifiedReleaseManifest`/`VerifiedReleaseAsset`) → Ed25519 over raw manifest
bytes → SHA-256 + declared size → two-phase archive preflight → `UpdatePlan` with
`UNKNOWN ⇒ DO NOT OVERWRITE` → `JOURNALED_TRANSACTIONAL_REPLACEMENT` + `.rollback` +
`update_transaction.json` → `HealthProof` → deterministic rollback → recovery from journal.
The term "Atomic Swap" is forbidden: multi-file replacement is *not power-loss atomic*,
it is *crash recoverable by journal*.

## 7. Linux support policy (binding, 2026-11-09)
- Minimum kernel: **Linux 7.2**, policy `OWNER_APPROVED_FIXED_MINIMUM` (supersedes the dynamic 6.12 floor).
- Minimum glibc: **2.43**; maximum allowed required symbol `GLIBC_2.43`; no bundled glibc; no rebuild to 2.41.
- Supported: Ubuntu 26.10, Fedora 45 Final/GA, current Arch, current openSUSE Tumbleweed.
- **Not supported: Debian 13.7 (standard configuration), openSUSE Leap.**
- Ubuntu 26.04 LTS: CONDITIONAL (kernel ≥ 7.2, glibc ≥ 2.43, official kernel source, native test, no unofficial repo).
- Requirement: `kernel >= 7.2 AND glibc >= 2.43 AND x86_64 AND successful native verification`.
- No manual system glibc replacement, no bundled glibc, no app-driven dependency installation.
- IMPORTANT: the repository still encodes the superseded 6.12 / 7-profile policy, and a guard test
  enforces it. Do not treat the current snapshot as authoritative and do not "fix" it casually —
  the change is scoped by `docs/NEXT_WORK_GATE.md`.

## 8. Data and platform invariants
XDG Base Directory on Linux (absolute paths or safe `$HOME` fallback), `%APPDATA%` on Windows,
SQLite WAL with online backup only, per-journal isolation, indexes from first install are seeds
(`NeverOverwrite`), uninstallers never delete user data, no writes beside the binary.

## 9. Reporting
Every gate produces a report with: date/environment, Git before/after, commit list,
files changed, commands + exact counters, findings with severity and `file:line`,
and the single next gate. No commit is made in an analysis-only phase.
````

**Why this status and not `READY_WITH_DOCUMENTATION_CORRECTIONS`:**
the owner's own stop rule (§28) freezes mutation when the baseline does not pass, and the
prescribed baseline command **does** fail — deterministically, from a hermeticity defect in one
test (`F-24`). The failure is not a product regression and the remedy is small and test-only,
but reporting "ready" while the prescribed command exits non-zero would be exactly the kind of
unverified claim this audit exists to prevent.

**If the owner decides that a non-hermetic installer E2E test does not constitute a blocking
baseline failure**, the status downgrades to `READY_WITH_DOCUMENTATION_CORRECTIONS` and the next
gate becomes `STAGE-M3-F-LINUX-SUPPORT-POLICY-ALIGNMENT-GATE` (§19.2), with F-24 moved to the
follow-up gate. This is an explicit owner decision, not an auditor's choice.
